entities.name: Acute ischemic stroke
observations: Disabling focal neurologic deficits began 1 hour ago; noncontrast CT shows no hemorrhage, glucose is 106 mg/dL, and BP is 145/90 mmHg.
IV alteplase is supported within 4.5 hours when no additional contraindication is present and BP is below 185/110 mmHg.

entities.name: Alteplase
observations: Immediate IV alteplase is recommended for this disabling acute ischemic stroke presentation; treatment should not await MRI or CTA if otherwise eligible.

entities.name: CT angiography
observations: Urgent CTA of the head and neck can identify large-vessel occlusion and thrombectomy eligibility, but should be performed in parallel without delaying alteplase.

entities.name: Aspirin
observations: Aspirin or other antiplatelet therapy should not be administered before IV alteplase; after thrombolysis, antithrombotics are generally withheld until follow-up imaging at about 24 hours excludes hemorrhage.

entities.name: Heparin
observations: Routine heparin is not recommended as acute ischemic stroke treatment or as a substitute for reperfusion because of bleeding risk.
